chunks: And God has favoured some of you over others in provision. But those who have been favoured do not return their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so they are equal in it. Do they then deny the favour of God?

key_terms.أَيْمَانُهُمْ: Their right hands (referring to dependents or slaves)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the distribution of wealth and gratitude towards God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted to distinguish between the natural hierarchy of provision (rizq) and the moral obligation of gratitude, emphasizing that material disparity does not imply spiritual inequality. The phrase 'what their right hands possess' is understood broadly to include all dependents, highlighting that while wealth distribution is divinely ordained, the denial of this grace constitutes a fundamental flaw in human recognition of God's bounty. This serves as a reminder that true equality lies in submission to God rather than uniformity of material status.
